result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers follow the brand closely: radius is zero with an optional round exception, depth comes from rules, there are no blurred shadows, and motion is close to none with reduced-motion handled. A is slightly tighter. Its raised and overlay roles are clearly defined, and it gives one ready-to-paste CSS block with an explicit reduced-motion remap. B adds useful practical points (the Safari radius reset, a focus ring, and the hard-offset-shadow decision), but it brings in a five-step z-index scale and an extra hairline rule weight, which makes its token set less minimal. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep radius at zero with a narrowly scoped round exception, use rules instead of blur for depth, and keep motion near zero. B is slightly better: it defines explicit flat, raised and overlay roles in the brand's own language, remaps its single duration under prefers-reduced-motion, and ends with a ready-to-paste CSS block and lint guidance. A is also strong, but it never clearly says what makes an element raised, its five-step z-index scale adds some padding, and its reduced-motion handling is thinner.
